sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the revisionist would be referred to as the 'accused' and Smt. Beena as the 'complainant' as per their nomenclature before the Trial Court.

BRIEF FACTS:
5.

Briefly stated, the facts relevant for the disposal of the present revision are that the accused purchased property bearing House No. G-4/237, G-4 Block, Sonia Vihar, Delhi (in short 'property in question') in the name of his wife from one Ashwani Kumar and constructed two rooms with a kitchen in the property.
He started residing in the said property with his family.
It is averred that it is the case of the complainant that she purchased the property in question on 20.02.1998 and allowed the accused to reside therein as a licensee in the year 2005.
It is averred that in the year 2013, when the accused did not vacate the property in question, a false case was got registered against him by the complainant.

In para 6 of the revision petition, it is averred as under:-
"6.

That revisionist has been residing on the property bearing H.No. G-4/237, G-4 Block, Delhi Police Side Panchva Pusta, Sonia Vihar, Delhi since 1996 as a owner and son of revisionist namely Pramod Kumar studied in SHRI RADHA KRISHAN Digitally signed by PRAVEEN RAM JATAN PUBLIC SCHOOL add-G-116, Main PRAVEEN KUMAR KUMAR Date:
2023.03.22 Road, Sonia Vihar, Delhi-110094 in the year 2003 and 16:07:07 +0530 at the time of admission the address H.No. G-4/237, G-4 Block, Delhi Police Side Panchva Pusta, Sonia Vihar, Delhi was given in the school and due to this reason revisionist filed an application for calling the Principal/Clerk of SHRI RADHA KRISHAN RAM JATAN PUBLIC SCHOOL add-G-116, Main Road, Sonia Vihar,
Delhi-110094 alongwith record of student Pramod Kumar to prove his defence that revisionist is residing on the address prior to 2005 but ld.

Trial Court did not appreciate it and dismissed the application."
ARGUMENTS:
6. I have heard Sh. Parveen Kumar, Ld. counsel for the revisionist; Sh. Mritunjai Singh, Ld. counsel for the complainant;
and Sh. Masood Ahmed, Ld. Addl. Public Prosecutor for the State.
7. Ld. counsel for the accused has contended that the accused is the owner of the property in question as the same was purchased by him in the year 1996.

However, to falsify the stand taken by the complainant that in the year 2005 accused was allowed to reside in the property in question as a licensee, the accused wants to examine a witness to prove that accused was in occupation of the property in question in the year 2003.
It is contended that the examination of the said witness is necessary for the just decision of the case and an opportunity be granted to the accused to prove his defence.

It is contended that the denial of examination of defence witness amounts to violation of principles of natural justice and, therefore, the order of the Trial Court is not sustainable under law.
8.
On the other hand, Ld. counsel for the complainant and Ld. Addl. P. P for the State has contended that there is no infirmity in the impugned order passed by the Trial Court.

sentences.text: 2 FINDINGS & DISCUSSION:
Digitally signed by PRAVEEN KUMAR Date: 2023.03.22 9.
I have gone through the record.

During the course of 16:07:17 +0530 arguments, Ld. counsel for the complainant has not disputed the fact that it is the case of the complainant that in the year 2005,
accused was allowed to reside in the property in question.
10. It is the basic principle of criminal law that in order to hold an accused guilty of an offence, all the ingredients of that offence should be established against him beyond reasonable doubt.
The burden upon accused is not so onerous and the standard expected of him is that of preponderance of probabilities by moving cogent and viable evidence.

11. Though not referred to or relied upon, in judgment- Krishna Janardhan Bhat Vs. Dutta Traya G.
Hegde, (2008) 4 SCC 54, the Apex Court has held as under:-
"Whereas prosecution must prove the guilt of an accused beyond all unreasonable doubt, the standard of proof as to prove a defence on part of the accused is preponderance of probabilities.

entities.text:
Krishna Janardhan Bhat Vs. Dutta Traya G.
Hegde, (2008) 4 SCC 54
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Inference of preponderance of probabilities can be drawn not only from the materials brought on records by the parties but also by reference to circumstances upon which he relies"
12.
Thus, the position on standard of proof is well settled.
The standard of proof on the part of an accused and that of the prosecution in a criminal case are different.
The standard of proof for an accused is preponderance of probabilities.

CONCLUSION:
13.

Considering the totality of facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that examination of the defence witness i.e Principal/Clerk of Shri Radha Krishan Ram Jatan Public School, G-116, Main Road, Sonia Vihar, Delhi-110094 is necessary for the just decision of the case.

The order dated 07.02.2023 passed by the Ld. +0530 ACMM, North-East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi is set-aside.
Revisionist be given an opportunity to examine the aforesaid defence witness.
